subject: research/free-f32bounce
professional: a computational dynamical-systems researcher (chaotic billiards, numerical shadowing); first checks: is the billiard map right (invariant-measure statistics against exact values), does the departure horizon scale as ln(1/eps)/lambda, is the per-member event-order claim actually what the data show, and is the result placed against the shadowing literature

evidence.correctness: Ran `PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 experiments/run.py` (5.4 s): output byte-identical to the committed experiments/results.txt (`diff ... && echo IDENTICAL` -> IDENTICAL). Independent pure-Python scalar billiard (/tmp/claude-0/audit-free-f32bounce/indep.py, no subject import, own seeds, 400 members x 4950 collisions) gives mean free path 0.45473 and circle share 0.2811 against the exact pi|Q|/|dQ| = 0.45321 and |circle|/|dQ| = 0.2820 (Chernov & Markarian, Chaotic Billiards, 2006); the subject's 0.45325/0.2821 agree. Subject vs independent float64 trajectories from the same 200 starts: identical surface sequence for 40 collisions in 191/200 members, position error 4.8e-14 over the first 10 (cross.py). An independent scalar float32 implementation (f32.py) departs from float64 at a median 21 collisions (q10-q90 17-25) and changes surface at a median 22, exactly the subject's headline. Refit of the five departure medians: a = -1.000, b = 1.3029, lambda = 0.7675, equivalent delta0 = 4.64e-8, as quoted. sqrt(n) drift of |d| checked: 2.63e-6 * sqrt(5) = 5.9e-6, * sqrt(20) = 1.18e-5 vs reported 5.83e-6 and 1.11e-5.
evidence.completeness: Every README deliverable reproduces: 10 tests pass (`python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, 0.2 s, README says ~1 s), run.py reproduces results.txt byte for byte, figure.py run in a scratch copy of research/_shared + the subject reproduces departure.svg byte for byte (cmp -> SVG-IDENTICAL). Dropped bouncing-ball attempt is disclosed, not shipped. Next steps listed as not done. Live page not loaded: curl to marisstella.app returned 000 through the proxy.
evidence.verification: 10 unit tests; 4 seeded mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: Cauchy denominator 2*pi*r -> pi*r caught; wall classification sid<=1 -> sid<1 caught; removing the circle self-exclusion (last != 4) survived (largely equivalent because of the b<0 guard, but the README calls exclusion load-bearing and no test exercises a near-tangent re-hit); flipping the sign of the intercept in the float32-equivalent-delta0 formula (experiments/run.py:43) survived: the headline number '~1x unit roundoff' has no test. Nothing tests experiments/run.py or the welch z.
evidence.craft: Read model.py (109 lines), run.py, figure.py, tests. Vectorised event-driven step is clear, dtype is held through every operation (checked: float32 path stays float32 until the float64 log cast). Small issues: __all__ (model.py:16) omits departure_index and surface_departure although `from .model import *` is the package API; pyproject.toml:8 still describes the dropped bouncing-ball project; Welch z (run.py:60) treats float32 and float64 ensembles from identical starts as independent samples (negligible over 2000 collisions, but a paired test is the right one).
evidence.claims: Numbers in the README all trace to results.txt (checked each headline figure). But README:14 says the surface change comes 'always exactly one collision after the position departure' and reads that as the signature of divergence-then-wrong-surface, adding 'I have not measured the reverse (a wrong surface chosen without position departure)'. That holds only for the medians. Per member (f32.py, 300 members, subject code): lag surface-minus-position = 1 in 84, 0 in 96, >=2 in 102, and negative in 18 (6%): the 'reverse' case occurs and is measurable with the subject's own arrays. pyproject description is stale (bouncing ball, 'impact statistics'). Citations are honestly flagged as from memory; disclaimer and AI note present.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun and extend it in seconds (numpy only, seeds fixed). Nearest prior work: numerical shadowing in chaotic systems (Hammel, Yorke & Grebogi 1987; Grebogi, Hammel, Yorke & Sauer, PRL 65, 1527, 1990) predicts both the ln(1/eps)/lambda departure horizon and that invariant statistics survive roundoff in hyperbolic systems; Lyapunov exponents of Sinai/Lorentz billiards are tabulated (e.g. Dellago, Posch & Hoover, PRE 53, 1485, 1996). None is cited, lambda = 0.77/collision is not compared to a published value, and 'statistics survive' is presented as a finding rather than the expected consequence. The new part (float32 ~ 1x unit roundoff here vs ~100x in the smooth flows of free-f32shadow) is a modest, sound observation, not a publishable result on its own.
evidence.domain: Method matches standard practice for billiard numerics: event-driven exact flights, specular reflection, exact invariant-measure checks (mean free path, boundary share), ensemble medians with q10-q90, a float64 perturbation ladder as the control. Departures: no per-time Lyapunov exponent or comparison to literature, departure threshold not varied (disclosed), surface exclusion not ablated (disclosed). A practitioner would sign off on the computation within its stated limits.

defects.what: Headline bullet says the event order changes 'always exactly one collision after the position departure' and that the reverse case was not measured; that is true of the ensemble medians only. Per member the lag is 0 in 32%, >=2 in 34%, and negative (surface changes before the 0.1 position departure) in 6%, measurable from the arrays run.py already has.
The headline float32-equivalent start error (fit inversion) and the Welch z are computed only in experiments/run.py with no test; flipping the intercept sign survives the suite.

Nearest prior work not cited: numerical shadowing (Grebogi, Hammel, Yorke & Sauer 1990) predicts both the ln(1/eps)/lambda horizon and survival of invariant statistics; billiard Lyapunov exponents are published (Dellago, Posch & Hoover 1996) but lambda = 0.77/collision is not compared.
Circle self-exclusion (README calls it load-bearing) is untested: removing `last != 4` leaves all tests green; no near-tangent re-hit test.
pyproject description still describes the dropped bouncing-ball project ('impact statistics').
__all__ omits departure_index and surface_departure, so the package-level `from .model import *` does not export the two analysis helpers run.py uses.
Welch z treats float32 and float64 ensembles run from identical starts as independent samples; a paired difference is the correct test (effect negligible here).

verdict: The numbers are right: results.txt and the figure reproduce byte for byte, and an independent pure-Python billiard reproduces the exact mean free path and circle share (Chernov & Markarian), the subject's float64 trajectories to 1e-14, and the float32 departure median of 21 collisions. It misses the bar on verification (the headline equivalence formula in run.py is untested; 2 of 4 seeded mutations survive) and claims (README:14's 'always exactly one collision after' holds only for medians; 6% of members change surface before the position departs, the case the README says it did not measure). Finished, sound within its stated limits, but a modest result that is not placed against the shadowing literature it largely restates.
